=== CALL C0350 ===
Laura: Hi. Can you hear me okay?
Darren: Yeah, got you. Darren.
Laura: Laura. Hi. Erm, so we just sort of chat for three minutes, I think.
Darren: Apparently. Not sure what they're after, to be honest, but go on. Did you finish that puzzle thing?
Laura: Most of it. I got stuck on the last couple of grids, the ones with the shapes. I ran out of time.
Darren: Same. Gave up on the last one, couldn't see it. Bit of a daft way to start, but there you go.
Laura: Yeah. So where are you, roughly?
Darren: Basingstoke. Brighton Hill.
Laura: Oh, really? I'm in Chineham.
Darren: No way. Small world. What d'you do then?
Laura: I'm a management accountant at a logistics company, on one of the estates out by the ring road. Monthly accounts, budgets for three depots, that sort of thing. It's month-end next week, so it's about to get a bit hectic.
Darren: Right. I'm on an estate too, the other side. I run a builders' merchant, branch manager. Nine in the yard, two on the counter.
Laura: Oh, okay. That's quite a lot of people.
Darren: Yeah. Had a delivery turn up two hours late this morning, so the yard was absolutely heaving. Trade lads stood about moaning, drivers moaning. So I'm a bit knackered, if I'm honest.
Laura: I bet. Do you do your own figures, or does head office do all that?
Darren: Bit of both. I do stock, shrinkage, all that. Head office does the quarterly review and picks it apart. You'd probably enjoy that bit more than me.
Laura: Ha, maybe. Usually I'm the one picking it apart, to be honest. Sorry.
Darren: Ha. Fair enough. Kids?
Laura: One, Alfie. He's six, Year 2. My mum does pick-up a couple of days, she's over in Tadley.
Darren: Funny. My lad's Alfie as well. He's nine. He's with his mum in Tadley, actually.
Laura: Oh, that's a coincidence. Two Alfies and Tadley.
Darren: Yeah. Er, I have him every other weekend and a night in the week. So... yeah.
Laura: That must be hard, the in-between bit.
Darren: It is what it is. I take him to Reading when I can, the football. He's more into it than I was at nine, to be fair.
Laura: My husband would get on with you then. He has the football on all the time and I sort of half watch.
Darren: Who's he support?
Laura: Erm, Reading, I think, mostly? He moans about them a lot.
Darren: Then he's definitely Reading. Everyone moans. Lost again Saturday. Owners don't have a clue.
Laura: That's exactly what he says.
Darren: Ha. Do you do anything at weekends then, or is it all kids' stuff?
Laura: I do parkrun on a Saturday, War Memorial Park. I'm on eighty-seven, I want to get to a hundred.
Darren: Eighty-seven? Blimey. My partner drags me to that now and again. I do weights, three mornings before work. Running kills my knee.
Laura: I'm not fast. About thirty-one minutes. It's more the routine, really, gets me out the house.
Darren: Thirty-one's alright. Better than me when I'm hanging off the back.
Laura: Well, if you come on a Saturday you can say hello.
Darren: Maybe. Kelly'll be made up if I volunteer to go for once.
Laura: Erm, what else... do you do the Friday takeaway thing as well? Everyone seems to.
Darren: Every Friday. Chicken madras, same place, never changes.
Laura: We're the same. I keep saying we should cut down and then it's Friday and—
Darren: And it's Friday, yeah. No chance.

=== CALL C0351 ===
Callum: Hey! There we go. Hi, I'm Callum.
Gemma: Hi, Gemma.
Callum: Gemma, nice one. How was the puzzle bit? I absolutely bombed that, I'm not gonna lie.
Gemma: It was fine. I finished it.
Callum: All of it? Fair play. I got to the shapes ones and my brain just sort of left the building. So what do you do, Gemma?
Gemma: New car sales. Franchised dealership in Basingstoke.
Callum: No way! Stop it. I'm in car sales. Used and nearly-new, outside Stevenage.
Gemma: Oh right. Funny. Used's a different game, though.
Callum: Yeah, yeah, totally different game. You've got the manufacturer behind you, the shiny showroom, all that. We've got a forecourt on an industrial estate and a bloke who does the valeting with a hose.
Gemma: We've got targets from the manufacturer on top of ours, so it's not exactly easy either. How are you doing this month?
Callum: Erm, decent, yeah. I'm usually near the top of the board. This month's a bit slow, to be honest, it's been quiet on the forecourt.
Gemma: I'm top this month. Second last month, by one car, which I'm still annoyed about.
Callum: By one car! That's brutal. Who beat you?
Gemma: New lad. He got a fleet deal handed to him, so it doesn't really count, to be fair.
Callum: It doesn't count, no, a handed fleet deal is basically cheating. I'd be fuming.
Gemma: I was.
Callum: Ha. Erm, so, do you do Saturdays? I'm six days most weeks, Saturdays are a killer.
Gemma: Alternate ones. I'm off this weekend, thank God.
Callum: Lucky. What do you do on your days off then? Let me guess, gym. I clocked the top in your photo.
Gemma: Gym, yeah, three times a week. Weights and rowing. And I walk the dog. I did the Basingstoke Half last year, two hours four.
Callum: Two hours four, that's proper. I couldn't do half of a half. I've been playing padel with a couple of lads from work, and honestly, mate, padel is way harder than it looks. You think it's just tennis for people who've given up, then you're on the floor.
Gemma: I've never played it.
Callum: You'd smash it, honestly, with the rowing and that. You'd have the arms for it.
Gemma: Maybe.
Callum: Yeah. Erm... so what are you watching at the minute? I watched this Korean thriller last night, it was unreal, like proper twisty, there's this—
Gemma: I don't really do subtitles. I'm watching The Traitors.
Callum: The Traitors, okay, yeah, everyone's on that.
Gemma: I'd win it. Honestly. It's just reading people, which is what we do all day.
Callum: That's a good shout, actually. We'd be well suited, car salespeople. You'd know straight away who's lying.
Gemma: I'd know who's lying in about five seconds, yeah.
Callum: Bit worrying for me, then.
Gemma: Is it?
Callum: Ha! No, no. I'm an open book. Ask my mum. Erm, do you reckon you'll stay in sales, or go for manager?
Gemma: Manager. If they don't give it me in the next couple of years I'll go to another group. I'm not loyal for the sake of it.
Callum: Nah, fair. Same, I'd love a premium brand, the commission on those—
Gemma: The commission's better, but the customers are worse.
Callum: The customers are worse, ha, I can imagine. I had a bloke yesterday test-drive a car just to get to Tesco—

=== CALL C0352 ===
Gillian: Hello. Can you see me? The angle's a bit odd, it's on the island.
Laura: Yes, I can see you fine. Hi, I'm Laura.
Gillian: Gillian. Erm, do you actually know what this is all for? They didn't really say.
Laura: Not really, no. Something about first impressions, I think. How people get on.
Gillian: Right. Well. As long as nobody's selling my details, that's all I care about.
Laura: Ha, yeah. So where are you based?
Gillian: Bramhall. Stockport, sort of South Manchester. It's a nice area. You?
Laura: Basingstoke. Chineham, on the edge of it.
Gillian: Oh, I don't know it. Is it nice?
Laura: It's fine. It's an estate, but it's quiet. Lakes nearby, that kind of thing.
Gillian: Mm. And what do you do?
Laura: I'm a management accountant. Logistics company, I do the monthly figures for three depots.
Gillian: Oh, right. I'm an optometrist. Three days a week, in Stockport town centre.
Laura: Oh, okay. So eye tests and that?
Gillian: Eye tests, eye health, referrals if something's not right. Which is fine, that's the job, I don't mind that bit. It's everything else. They've got targets now for selling glasses, add-ons, coatings, and the manager stands there watching while you're trying to talk someone through a cataract. And parking in Stockport is a nightmare, so I'm already wound up by the time I get in. I'm shattered after a Tuesday, honestly. Erm, yeah, that's it really.
Laura: I can imagine. We've got targets too, but they're more cost ones. I'm usually the one telling people their numbers don't add up.
Gillian: I bet that makes you popular.
Laura: Ha, not massively. I try to just quietly fix it, to be honest.
Gillian: Sensible. Have you got kids?
Laura: One, Alfie. He's six. He's just started swimming lessons on a Tuesday, so that's my Tuesday gone as well.
Gillian: Oh, I remember all that. Mine are grown up now. Son's in Leeds, daughter's at uni in Nottingham. She rings when she needs money, which is most weeks.
Laura: Is it quiet with them both gone?
Gillian: Erm... it's quieter. We've got the dog, so. Bella. She's down there somewhere. She needs her nails doing and the groomer wants forty-five pound, which is daylight robbery.
Laura: Forty-five? For nails?
Gillian: For a full groom. But still. I'm not paying it just for her nails, do you know what I mean?
Laura: No, fair enough. We've got a cat, he just gets fat and is sick on the rug.
Gillian: Ha. Lovely.
Laura: Erm, so what do you do on your days off?
Gillian: Walk Bella round the park. Pool and sauna at the gym. Telly. Married at First Sight with a glass of wine, I'm not going to pretend otherwise.
Laura: Ha, I watch Bake Off. And Gogglebox.
Gillian: Oh, Gogglebox is good. Martin, my husband, hates it, so I put it on while I'm doing tea.
Laura: Tea as in dinner?
Gillian: Yeah, tea. Half six. Sorry, northern.
Laura: No, it's fine. I'm dinner. My nan said tea, actually.
Gillian: There you go. Your nan had it right.
Laura: Maybe. Erm, do you get away much?
Gillian: Algarve most summers, same villa complex. I don't like flying, so I go where I know. Last time we did Rome, five-star, lovely hotel.
Laura: We're the same, really. Cornwall three years running. I like to know what I'm getting.
Gillian: Exactly. People think it's boring. It's not boring, it's just—

Darren: Right. Saturdays?
Callum: Six days, mate. Saturdays are the worst, I'm knackered by the Sunday.

Darren: Reading.
Callum: Oh. Erm. Sorry.

Darren: Nine. Alfie. He's with his mum mostly, so I take him when I've got him. He loves it, even when they're rubbish.

Darren: Three mornings a week, weights. My dad had a heart attack at fifty-eight, so.
Callum: Oh, mate, sorry. Is he okay?
Darren: He's alright now. Watches what he eats, sort of. Friday's still a curry, mind.

Laura: No way. So's Dan. He runs a little business with one other bloke.

Laura: Just his surname, really. Dan Hollis Electrical. Very imaginative.
Gemma: I'll ask him. They all end up in the same builders' merchant anyway.
Laura: Probably Darren's.
Gemma: Ha, probably. Have you got any other kids?
Laura: Erm, no. Just Alfie. You?
Gemma: No. Just the dog. And a garden room Craig's been building since about March.
Laura: Dan's been meaning to do our fence since spring. I've given up asking.
Gemma: Give him a deadline. Works with Craig. Sort of.
Laura: Ha. Do you run? You look quite sporty.
Gemma: Gym mostly. I did the Basingstoke Half once. Two hours four.
Laura: Oh, well done. I just do parkrun. War Memorial Park. I'm on eighty-seven.
Gemma: Eighty-seven? That's a lot of Saturdays.
Laura: It is. I want to get to a hundred, then I get the t-shirt.
Gemma: What's your time?
Laura: About thirty-one minutes. I'm not quick.
Gemma: Eighty-seven, though. That's consistency. That's worth more than speed, to be fair.

calls.C0350:
Laura: Hi. Can you hear me okay?
Darren: Yeah, got you. Darren.
Laura: Laura. Hi. Erm, so we just sort of chat for three minutes, I think.
Darren: Apparently. Not sure what they're after, to be honest, but go on. Did you finish that puzzle thing?
Laura: Most of it. I got stuck on the last couple of grids, the ones with the shapes. I ran out of time.
Darren: Same. Gave up on the last one, couldn't see it. Bit of a daft way to start, but there you go.
Laura: Yeah. So where are you, roughly?
Darren: Basingstoke. Brighton Hill.
Laura: Oh, really? I'm in Chineham.
Darren: No way. Small world. What d'you do then?
Laura: I'm a management accountant at a logistics company, on one of the estates out by the ring road. Monthly accounts, budgets for three depots, that sort of thing. It's month-end next week, so it's about to get a bit hectic.
Darren: Right. I'm on an estate too, the other side. I run a builders' merchant, branch manager. Nine in the yard, two on the counter.
Laura: Oh, okay. That's quite a lot of people.
Darren: Yeah. Had a delivery turn up two hours late this morning, so the yard was absolutely heaving. Trade lads stood about moaning, drivers moaning. So I'm a bit knackered, if I'm honest.
Laura: I bet. Do you do your own figures, or does head office do all that?
Darren: Bit of both. I do stock, shrinkage, all that. Head office does the quarterly review and picks it apart. You'd probably enjoy that bit more than me.
Laura: Ha, maybe. Usually I'm the one picking it apart, to be honest. Sorry.
Darren: Ha. Fair enough. Kids?
Laura: One, Alfie. He's six, Year 2. My mum does pick-up a couple of days, she's over in Tadley.
Darren: Funny. My lad's Alfie as well. He's nine. He's with his mum in Tadley, actually.
Laura: Oh, that's a coincidence. Two Alfies and Tadley.
Darren: Yeah. Er, I have him every other weekend and a night in the week. So... yeah.
Laura: That must be hard, the in-between bit.
Darren: It is what it is. I take him to Reading when I can, the football. He's more into it than I was at nine, to be fair.
Laura: My husband would get on with you then. He has the football on all the time and I sort of half watch.
Darren: Who's he support?
Laura: Erm, Reading, I think, mostly? He moans about them a lot.
Darren: Then he's definitely Reading. Everyone moans. Lost again Saturday. Owners don't have a clue.
Laura: That's exactly what he says.
Darren: Ha. Do you do anything at weekends then, or is it all kids' stuff?
Laura: I do parkrun on a Saturday, War Memorial Park. I'm on eighty-seven, I want to get to a hundred.
Darren: Eighty-seven? Blimey. My partner drags me to that now and again. I do weights, three mornings before work. Running kills my knee.
Laura: I'm not fast. About thirty-one minutes. It's more the routine, really, gets me out the house.
Darren: Thirty-one's alright. Better than me when I'm hanging off the back.
Laura: Well, if you come on a Saturday you can say hello.
Darren: Maybe. Kelly'll be made up if I volunteer to go for once.
Laura: Erm, what else... do you do the Friday takeaway thing as well? Everyone seems to.
Darren: Every Friday. Chicken madras, same place, never changes.
Laura: We're the same. I keep saying we should cut down and then it's Friday and—
Darren: And it's Friday, yeah. No chance.
calls.C0351:
Callum: Hey! There we go. Hi, I'm Callum.
Gemma: Hi, Gemma.
Callum: Gemma, nice one. How was the puzzle bit? I absolutely bombed that, I'm not gonna lie.
Gemma: It was fine. I finished it.
Callum: All of it? Fair play. I got to the shapes ones and my brain just sort of left the building. So what do you do, Gemma?
Gemma: New car sales. Franchised dealership in Basingstoke.
Callum: No way! Stop it. I'm in car sales. Used and nearly-new, outside Stevenage.
Gemma: Oh right. Funny. Used's a different game, though.
Callum: Yeah, yeah, totally different game. You've got the manufacturer behind you, the shiny showroom, all that. We've got a forecourt on an industrial estate and a bloke who does the valeting with a hose.
Gemma: We've got targets from the manufacturer on top of ours, so it's not exactly easy either. How are you doing this month?
Callum: Erm, decent, yeah. I'm usually near the top of the board. This month's a bit slow, to be honest, it's been quiet on the forecourt.
Gemma: I'm top this month. Second last month, by one car, which I'm still annoyed about.
Callum: By one car! That's brutal. Who beat you?
Gemma: New lad. He got a fleet deal handed to him, so it doesn't really count, to be fair.
Callum: It doesn't count, no, a handed fleet deal is basically cheating. I'd be fuming.
Gemma: I was.
Callum: Ha. Erm, so, do you do Saturdays? I'm six days most weeks, Saturdays are a killer.
Gemma: Alternate ones. I'm off this weekend, thank God.
Callum: Lucky. What do you do on your days off then? Let me guess, gym. I clocked the top in your photo.
Gemma: Gym, yeah, three times a week. Weights and rowing. And I walk the dog. I did the Basingstoke Half last year, two hours four.
Callum: Two hours four, that's proper. I couldn't do half of a half. I've been playing padel with a couple of lads from work, and honestly, mate, padel is way harder than it looks. You think it's just tennis for people who've given up, then you're on the floor.
Gemma: I've never played it.
Callum: You'd smash it, honestly, with the rowing and that. You'd have the arms for it.
Gemma: Maybe.
Callum: Yeah. Erm... so what are you watching at the minute? I watched this Korean thriller last night, it was unreal, like proper twisty, there's this—
Gemma: I don't really do subtitles. I'm watching The Traitors.
Callum: The Traitors, okay, yeah, everyone's on that.
Gemma: I'd win it. Honestly. It's just reading people, which is what we do all day.
Callum: That's a good shout, actually. We'd be well suited, car salespeople. You'd know straight away who's lying.
Gemma: I'd know who's lying in about five seconds, yeah.
Callum: Bit worrying for me, then.
Gemma: Is it?
Callum: Ha! No, no. I'm an open book. Ask my mum. Erm, do you reckon you'll stay in sales, or go for manager?
Gemma: Manager. If they don't give it me in the next couple of years I'll go to another group. I'm not loyal for the sake of it.
Callum: Nah, fair. Same, I'd love a premium brand, the commission on those—
Gemma: The commission's better, but the customers are worse.
Callum: The customers are worse, ha, I can imagine. I had a bloke yesterday test-drive a car just to get to Tesco—
calls.C0352:
Gillian: Hello. Can you see me? The angle's a bit odd, it's on the island.
Laura: Yes, I can see you fine. Hi, I'm Laura.
Gillian: Gillian. Erm, do you actually know what this is all for? They didn't really say.
Laura: Not really, no. Something about first impressions, I think. How people get on.
Gillian: Right. Well. As long as nobody's selling my details, that's all I care about.
Laura: Ha, yeah. So where are you based?
Gillian: Bramhall. Stockport, sort of South Manchester. It's a nice area. You?
Laura: Basingstoke. Chineham, on the edge of it.
Gillian: Oh, I don't know it. Is it nice?
Laura: It's fine. It's an estate, but it's quiet. Lakes nearby, that kind of thing.
Gillian: Mm. And what do you do?
Laura: I'm a management accountant. Logistics company, I do the monthly figures for three depots.
Gillian: Oh, right. I'm an optometrist. Three days a week, in Stockport town centre.
Laura: Oh, okay. So eye tests and that?
Gillian: Eye tests, eye health, referrals if something's not right. Which is fine, that's the job, I don't mind that bit. It's everything else. They've got targets now for selling glasses, add-ons, coatings, and the manager stands there watching while you're trying to talk someone through a cataract. And parking in Stockport is a nightmare, so I'm already wound up by the time I get in. I'm shattered after a Tuesday, honestly. Erm, yeah, that's it really.
Laura: I can imagine. We've got targets too, but they're more cost ones. I'm usually the one telling people their numbers don't add up.
Gillian: I bet that makes you popular.
Laura: Ha, not massively. I try to just quietly fix it, to be honest.
Gillian: Sensible. Have you got kids?
Laura: One, Alfie. He's six. He's just started swimming lessons on a Tuesday, so that's my Tuesday gone as well.
Gillian: Oh, I remember all that. Mine are grown up now. Son's in Leeds, daughter's at uni in Nottingham. She rings when she needs money, which is most weeks.
Laura: Is it quiet with them both gone?
Gillian: Erm... it's quieter. We've got the dog, so. Bella. She's down there somewhere. She needs her nails doing and the groomer wants forty-five pound, which is daylight robbery.
Laura: Forty-five? For nails?
Gillian: For a full groom. But still. I'm not paying it just for her nails, do you know what I mean?
Laura: No, fair enough. We've got a cat, he just gets fat and is sick on the rug.
Gillian: Ha. Lovely.
Laura: Erm, so what do you do on your days off?
Gillian: Walk Bella round the park. Pool and sauna at the gym. Telly. Married at First Sight with a glass of wine, I'm not going to pretend otherwise.
Laura: Ha, I watch Bake Off. And Gogglebox.
Gillian: Oh, Gogglebox is good. Martin, my husband, hates it, so I put it on while I'm doing tea.
Laura: Tea as in dinner?
Gillian: Yeah, tea. Half six. Sorry, northern.
Laura: No, it's fine. I'm dinner. My nan said tea, actually.
Gillian: There you go. Your nan had it right.
Laura: Maybe. Erm, do you get away much?
Gillian: Algarve most summers, same villa complex. I don't like flying, so I go where I know. Last time we did Rome, five-star, lovely hotel.
Laura: We're the same, really. Cornwall three years running. I like to know what I'm getting.
Gillian: Exactly. People think it's boring. It's not boring, it's just—
calls.C0353:
Callum: Hey, hey! Alright? Callum.
Darren: Alright, mate. Darren.
Callum: Darren, nice one. Love the polo, very official. Are you on your lunch or finished?
Darren: Finished. Just got in. What're we meant to be talking about, d'you know?
Callum: No idea, mate, just chatting, I think. I just had a girl from Basingstoke, Gemma, she was nice. Bit scary.
Darren: I'm Basingstoke. Brighton Hill.
Callum: No way! You lot are everywhere. Is it all car sales down there? She was car sales. I'm car sales.
Darren: Builders' merchant. I run a branch. Yard, trade counter, deliveries.
Callum: Oh, proper. So like timber, bricks, all that?
Darren: Timber, aggregates, plasterboard, the lot. Had a delivery two hours late this morning and half the town's builders stood in my yard moaning at me, so. Not the best start.
Callum: Two hours! What do you even do with them?
Darren: Tell the driver what I think of him. Then deal with the lads. It's not complicated, it just shouldn't happen.
Callum: Ha, I bet. We get that with transporters, car turns up a day late and the customer thinks I've done it on purpose. I'm in Stevenage, by the way, used and nearly-new.
Darren: Right. Saturdays?
Callum: Six days, mate. Saturdays are the worst, I'm knackered by the Sunday.
Darren: Same, I do every other one. Who d'you support, then? You've got an Arsenal mug there.
Callum: You clocked it! Yeah, Arsenal, through my dad. You?
Darren: Reading.
Callum: Oh. Erm. Sorry.
Darren: Yeah, don't. Lost again Saturday. The owners haven't got a clue, the manager's out of his depth, and every year we're told it's a rebuild. I used to have a season ticket. Now I just go a few times a year with my lad.
Callum: How old's your lad?
Darren: Nine. Alfie. He's with his mum mostly, so I take him when I've got him. He loves it, even when they're rubbish.
Callum: That's nice, though. That's what it's about, innit. Ha, sorry, I don't know why I said innit. My dad used to take me to the Emirates, still does sometimes, if someone's got a spare.
Darren: Yeah. It's good to have that. Erm, yeah. So, cars. Do you ever get deals or is that a myth?
Callum: Ha, it depends who's asking, mate. For you, I'd be honest.
Darren: Would you?
Callum: Mostly! No, I would. Honestly, finance on used, it's all in the APR. People look at the monthly and not the total. That's the bit you want to watch.
Darren: That's what I thought. I've got a car loan now, I'm not looking at it too hard.
Callum: Yeah, you and me both, mate. Mine's a bit much, if I'm honest. Erm, what do you do to switch off, then? Gym? You look like a gym man.
Darren: Three mornings a week, weights. My dad had a heart attack at fifty-eight, so.
Callum: Oh, mate, sorry. Is he okay?
Darren: He's alright now. Watches what he eats, sort of. Friday's still a curry, mind.
Callum: Got to keep Friday. I've been doing padel, way harder than it looks, you'd—
calls.C0354:
Gemma: Hi. Gemma.
Gillian: Hello. Gillian. Sorry, the laptop's on the island, it's at a funny angle.
Gemma: You're fine. Nice kitchen.
Gillian: Thank you. Had it redone two years ago. Erm, do you know what they're actually doing with all this? The ratings and that?
Gemma: No idea. First impressions, I think. Whether they match up.
Gillian: Mm. I'd just like to know who's looking at it.
Gemma: Fair.
Gillian: So, erm... where are you?
Gemma: Basingstoke. Chineham.
Gillian: Oh, the other lady was Chineham. Laura?
Gemma: Was she? Didn't know that. Haven't had her yet. Where are you?
Gillian: Bramhall. Stockport. It's a nice area, South Manchester. I'm an optometrist, in Stockport town centre, three days a week.
Gemma: Oh, eyes. Do you like it?
Gillian: The clinical bit's fine. It's the selling I can't stand. They've got targets now for frames, coatings, anti-glare, the lot, and the manager hovers about while you're trying to tell someone they've got early glaucoma. It's not what I trained for, do you know what I mean? I trained to look after people's eyes, not to flog them a blue-light filter they don't need.
Gemma: I sell cars. New cars. So I'm probably the manager in that story.
Gillian: Oh. Right.
Gemma: I just mean, to be fair, someone's got to pay for the building, yeah? If the customer's happy and you've told them the truth, I don't see the problem with an add-on.
Gillian: Well. It depends if they need it.
Gemma: Sure.
Gillian: Erm, yeah. That's it really.
Gemma: Do you do Saturdays?
Gillian: No. And I'm not going to. They keep hinting, but I've done my time with Saturdays.
Gemma: I do alternate ones. I don't mind them, Saturday's where the money is.
Gillian: I suppose in your job, yeah.
Gemma: Is that your dog? Bottom of the screen?
Gillian: Bella. Cockapoo. She's flat out. She needs her nails doing and the groomer wants forty-five pound for a full groom, which I think is daylight robbery.
Gemma: Haggle. Honestly. Say you'll go somewhere else.
Gillian: I did, actually. Got five off.
Gemma: There you go. I've got a spaniel, Dexter. He rolled in fox poo this morning on the walk, so that was my seven o'clock sorted.
Gillian: Oh, God. Bella did that once at Bramhall Park. Never again.
Gemma: Stinks for days.
Gillian: Days. Martin wouldn't let her in the lounge. Erm, have you got kids?
Gemma: No.
Gillian: Right.
Gemma: Just Dexter. And my husband's building a garden room, so that's basically a child.
Gillian: Ha. Our neighbours had an extension done and it's blocked all the light in the side of the kitchen. They didn't even ask. Well, they had planning, but they didn't ask us. I'm still annoyed about it, if I'm honest.
Gemma: Did you object?
Gillian: Martin said leave it. I should've objected.
Gemma: You should've. I'd have been round there.
Gillian: That's what I said. Anyway. What are you doing for tea tonight, then? Sorry, dinner.
Gemma: Chicken and rice. Craig does the cooking. Friday's a takeaway.
Gillian: Indian?
Gemma: Indian or Nando's.
Gillian: Indian, us. Same place every week. I'm not fussed about trying new places, I like what I like.
Gemma: Same. I don't do those places with tiny portions on a slate.
Gillian: Oh, no. Slates. Give it me on a plate, I'm not a goat.
Gemma: Ha. Yeah.
Gillian: Erm, do you get away much?
Gemma: Twice a year. Tenerife, Turkey. I always ask for an upgrade at check-in. Nine times out of ten you get one if you complain properly.
Gillian: I'm the same with refunds. If something's wrong, I say so. People don't, and then they moan after.
Gemma: Exactly. You just have to be—
calls.C0355:
Callum: Hello! Hi, I'm Callum. Can you hear me alright?
Gillian: Yes, fine. Gillian.
Callum: Gillian, nice to meet you. Ooh, is that a kitchen island? Very fancy.
Gillian: Thank you. It's new-ish. Two years. Erm, sorry, do you know what this study's actually for? Nobody's said.
Callum: Honestly, no idea. I think they just want to see if we all get on. I've had three so far and I've got on with everyone, so I'm smashing it.
Gillian: Right. Well done.
Callum: Ha. So where are you, Gillian?
Gillian: Bramhall. Near Stockport. It's a nice area. I'm an optometrist, I do three days in Stockport town centre.
Callum: Oh, an optician! My mum's always on at me to get my eyes tested, I squint at the telly.
Gillian: You should. If you're squinting, get it checked. It's probably just a prescription but you don't know, do you, and people leave things far too long. I had a man last month who'd had a curtain over one eye for a week and he'd just carried on driving. A week. Ended up in hospital that afternoon. Erm, yeah. Get it checked.
Callum: Okay, okay, I'm booking it, I promise. That's grim, a whole week.
Gillian: People don't think about their eyes until they've gone.
Callum: Yeah, fair. I'm in car sales, so I'm the opposite, I just look at bodywork all day. Used and nearly-new, outside Stevenage.
Gillian: Oh, you and the girl from Basingstoke, then. Gemma.
Callum: Yeah, Gemma! She's top of her board, she made sure I knew.
Gillian: She did seem quite... sure of herself.
Callum: Ha, that's diplomatic. Erm, is that a wine bottle behind you? Have you got one open?
Gillian: Not yet. That's for later. Married at First Sight's on.
Callum: Oh, my mum loves that. She watches it with my dad, he pretends he's not watching it.
Gillian: Martin's the same. Do you live near your mum, then?
Callum: Erm, I'm actually back at my mum and dad's at the minute. Saving for a deposit. Sort of.
Gillian: Oh. Well, a lot of them are, aren't they. My daughter'll be back after uni, I expect, she's already ringing for money every week.
Callum: Ha, yeah. I pay board, to be fair. Most months.
Gillian: Most months.
Callum: Most months! Don't tell my mum. Erm, so what's Martin into, then? Football?
Gillian: City. He has it on all the time, I sort of half listen.
Callum: Oh no, City. I'm Arsenal. Tell Martin I'm sorry for him, actually, no, tell him I'm jealous.
Gillian: I'll pass it on. He'll be insufferable.
Callum: Ha. Do you watch films at all? I'm a bit of a film nerd. I watched this Korean thriller last night, it was unreal.
Gillian: I don't really do arty films. I find them boring, if I'm honest. I like a crime drama on ITV, something where you know who did it by the end.
Callum: No, that's fair, that's fair. This one you do know who did it. Sort of. Eventually.
Gillian: Mm.
Callum: Okay, I'll stop selling it to you. Old habits.
calls.C0356:
Darren: Alright. Darren.
Gemma: Hi. Gemma. You're Basingstoke, aren't you? Callum said.
Darren: Brighton Hill. You?
Gemma: Chineham. What do you do?
Darren: Branch manager. Builders' merchant on the estate out past the ring road.
Gemma: Which one?
Darren: The one by the tip.
Gemma: Oh, I know it. My husband's an electrician, Craig, self-employed. He's probably been in.
Darren: Probably. Most of them come in for something. Moaning, usually.
Gemma: That sounds like Craig.
Darren: Ha. You're cars, Callum said.
Gemma: New cars, franchise on the retail park. I'm top of the board this month.
Darren: Right. Good for you.
Gemma: Do you have targets?
Darren: Head office figures. Stock, margin, shrinkage. Quarterly review's coming up, so they'll be picking it apart. I'm going for area manager, so it matters a bit more this time.
Gemma: Oh, same. Well, sales manager. If they don't give it me in a couple of years I'll move.
Darren: My problem's the meetings. Half the people who get promoted are just good at talking in meetings. I'd rather get the job done, to be honest.
Gemma: You need both, though, yeah? If nobody upstairs knows you're getting it done, it doesn't count.
Darren: Maybe. Not sure I agree, but go on.
Gemma: I just mean, put your numbers in front of them. Don't wait for them to notice. They won't.
Darren: Yeah. Fair enough, I suppose.
Gemma: What do you drive?
Darren: Er, company van in the week. I've got a car on finance. Needs its MOT booking, I keep forgetting.
Gemma: When it's up for renewal, come and see me. I'll sort you out.
Darren: That's what Callum said. Not sure I trust either of you.
Gemma: You shouldn't trust Callum. You can trust me.
Darren: Ha. Right. What d'you do weekends, then?
Gemma: Gym, three times a week. Weights, rowing. You?
Darren: Same, three mornings. Weights. Knee's gone for running.
Gemma: I did the Basingstoke Half last year. Two hours four.
Darren: Kelly drags me to parkrun. I'm at the back. Erm, yeah, so... Friday curry?
Gemma: Indian or Nando's. Craig decides.
Darren: Chicken madras. Every week.
Gemma: Every week? You don't fancy something else?
Darren: No. Why would I?
calls.C0357:
Darren: Alright. Darren.
Gillian: Hello. Gillian. Is this the last one?
Darren: Think so. Thank God. How long's it been, an hour?
Gillian: About that. Erm, I still don't really know what it's for.
Darren: No, me neither. Not sure what they're after, to be honest. Where are you, then?
Gillian: Bramhall. Stockport. It's a nice area. You're Basingstoke, I think. Everyone seems to be Basingstoke.
Darren: Yeah, half of them are. Brighton Hill. I run a builders' merchant.
Gillian: Oh, right. I'm an optometrist. Three days a week.
Darren: Eyes. Right. I should probably get mine done. Never have.
Gillian: Never? How old are you?
Darren: Thirty-six.
Gillian: Then go. It's not just glasses, it's eye health, blood pressure shows up in the back of your eye, diabetes, all sorts. Men your age never come in until something's wrong, and then it's, oh, I've had this headache for three weeks. You'd be surprised what we pick up. Erm, yeah. Sorry. Go and get it done.
Darren: Alright, alright. I'll book it. With the MOT.
Gillian: Ha. Do both.
Darren: Blood pressure, though. My dad had a heart attack at fifty-eight. So that's, er... that's why I go the gym, mostly.
Gillian: Oh. Martin's dad had one too. My husband. And Martin likes a drink, so I do worry, if I'm honest.
Darren: Does he do anything? Exercise?
Gillian: He watches City. Does that count?
Darren: Not really, no.
Gillian: No. That's what I tell him.
Darren: Yeah. Erm, yeah, so... you away this year?
Gillian: Algarve. Same place we always go. I hate flying, though. I'm a nightmare at the airport, I check the passports every five minutes.
Darren: Same. I check them about four times before we leave the house. Kelly goes mad.
Gillian: Martin says I'll wear the pages out.
Darren: Ha. We do Tenerife. All-inclusive. Sunbed, pool, done. I don't want to be traipsing round looking at churches.
Gillian: No. We did Rome once, it was a lovely hotel, five-star, but the walking. My feet.
Darren: That's why I don't do city breaks. Don't see the point.
Gillian: Erm, have you got kids? Sorry, I've asked everyone that.
Darren: A lad, Alfie, nine. He's with his mum. I have him every other weekend.
Gillian: Oh. That's hard.
Darren: Yeah. It is. Erm. He's good, though. Into his football.
Gillian: Mine have both gone now, so I'm sort of rattling round the house. Leeds and Nottingham.
Darren: Quiet, then.
Gillian: Very. Just me and the dog on my days off. Erm, yeah. That's it really.
Darren: Yeah, so... what you having for dinner?
Gillian: Tea? Spag bol, probably. Half six.
Darren: Tea, yeah. You lot. We're spag bol midweek too.
Gillian: Well, there you go. Something in common. Apart from the passports.
calls.C0358:
Laura: Hi. Laura.
Gemma: Hi, Gemma. You're Chineham, aren't you? Gillian said.
Laura: Yes, by the lakes. Are you too?
Gemma: Yeah, the newer bit. I walk the dog round the lakes most mornings.
Laura: Oh, I've probably seen you, then. Cocker spaniel?
Gemma: Dexter. If you saw one covered in fox poo this morning, that was him.
Laura: Ha. No, I missed that. So what do you do?
Gemma: New car sales. The franchise on the retail park. You?
Laura: Management accountant, logistics. I do the monthly accounts and budgets for three depots.
Gemma: Oh, numbers. Do you enjoy it?
Laura: I do, actually. I like month-end when it all ties up. I've got a checklist I've been tweaking for six years. Sounds a bit sad, I know.
Gemma: No, that's how you get things right. I've got a lad at work who can't fill in a finance form without three goes. I'd kill for someone with a checklist.
Laura: I'd be happy to lend it you. I'm not sure it'd cover car finance, though.
Gemma: Ha. Do you want to go further? Financial controller or whatever?
Laura: Erm, maybe. In a few years. I'm not desperate. Alfie's six, so I want to keep it sensible.
Gemma: I'd just go for it. If you're the one getting it right, make sure they know it. People like you get overlooked because you don't shout.
Laura: Maybe. I don't really like shouting, to be honest.
Gemma: You don't have to shout. Just put it in front of them.
Laura: Yeah. Fair point. Erm, what does your husband do?
Gemma: Craig's an electrician. Self-employed.
Laura: No way. So's Dan. He runs a little business with one other bloke.
Gemma: Seriously? Craig might know him. What's the business called?
Laura: Just his surname, really. Dan Hollis Electrical. Very imaginative.
Gemma: I'll ask him. They all end up in the same builders' merchant anyway.
Laura: Probably Darren's.
Gemma: Ha, probably. Have you got any other kids?
Laura: Erm, no. Just Alfie. You?
Gemma: No. Just the dog. And a garden room Craig's been building since about March.
Laura: Dan's been meaning to do our fence since spring. I've given up asking.
Gemma: Give him a deadline. Works with Craig. Sort of.
Laura: Ha. Do you run? You look quite sporty.
Gemma: Gym mostly. I did the Basingstoke Half once. Two hours four.
Laura: Oh, well done. I just do parkrun. War Memorial Park. I'm on eighty-seven.
Gemma: Eighty-seven? That's a lot of Saturdays.
Laura: It is. I want to get to a hundred, then I get the t-shirt.
Gemma: What's your time?
Laura: About thirty-one minutes. I'm not quick.
Gemma: Eighty-seven, though. That's consistency. That's worth more than speed, to be fair.

C0356.line_text: Gemma: I just mean, put your numbers in front of them. Don't wait for them to notice. They won't.
C0356.what: A brown-and-white cocker spaniel walks into the bottom right of Gemma's frame, picks the tennis ball out of the grey dog bed in its mouth and trots back out of shot, while Gemma keeps talking and doesn't look round.
